answer: We model Sybil resistance via a dynamic opportunity-cost bond where identities must commit staking collateral verified by a zero-knowledge delay function. When the slashing delta exceeds the maximum payoff of identity multiplication, any adversarial gale of coordinated Sybils is disincentivized. This mechanism extinguishes the malicious ember of collusion before payoff distribution, guaranteeing a negative expected utility and enforcing a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium where honest strategy dominates.
